newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA C.BANK NEEDS CAUTIOUS MONETARY POLICY-IMF.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA C.BANK NEEDS CAUTIOUS MONETARY POLICY-IMF.

text.p: Romania's Central Bank should pursue a gradual easing of monetary policy in the second half of the year as part of efforts to sustain market reforms, the IMF's chief negotiator for the country said on Thursday.

"The central bank is now facing the difficult task of having to ease monetary policy somewhat. There are signs that there is scope for easing monetary policy. But how much? Very cautious, gradual." Poul Thomsen said in an interview.
"I believe that the monetary policy that the central bank has in mind is prudent. It's not too fast."

After the election of a centrist government late last year, the central bank tightened monetary policy, pushing up interest rates and draining liquidity from the money market to help bring down inflation.

With monthly inflation slowing from a record 30.7 percent in March to an expected less than two percent last month, interest rates have slid sharply from peaks of 190-200 percent to about 30 percent on the money market.
The leu has stabilised at just over 7,000 to the dollar after falling to 9,000 in mid-February, when the local foreign exchange market was liberalised.
Central Bank governor Mugur Isarescu reiterated in an interview published this week he intended to proceed cautiously with easing policy.
"Relaxation of monetary constraints will be moderate in a process of something like a soft landing," he told the monthly Piata Financiara.
